canonical_statement: ADVANCE evaluated whether targeting glycated hemoglobin to 6.5% or less with an intensive glucose-control strategy reduced major vascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ADVANCE trial was designed to assess the effects on major vascular outcomes of lowering the glycated hemoglobin value to a target of 6.5% or less.

canonical_statement: Eligible participants had type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age 30 years or older, were at least 55 years old at study entry, and had major macrovascular or microvascular disease or at least one other vascular risk factor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Eligibility criteria... were a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus at 30 years of age or older, an age of at least 55 years... and a history of major macrovascular or microvascular disease or at least one other risk factor for vascular disease.

population.label: ADVANCE eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: Type 2 diabetes diagnosed at age >=30 years
History of major macrovascular or microvascular disease or at least one other vascular risk factor

canonical_statement: ADVANCE was a factorial randomized controlled trial conducted at 215 centers in 20 countries; central computer-based randomization allocated 11,140 participants to intensive or standard glucose-control strategies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ADVANCE trial is a factorial randomized, controlled trial conducted at 215 collaborating centers in 20 countries.

canonical_statement: The intensive-control arm used gliclazide modified release 30-120 mg daily, discontinued other sulfonylureas, and added other glucose-lowering treatments as required to target glycated hemoglobin <=6.5%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients who were randomly assigned to undergo intensive glucose control were given gliclazide (modified release, 30 to 120 mg daily)...

concept.text: Gliclazide modified release-based intensive glucose-control strategy

exposures.details: Other glucose-lowering drugs were added as required; other sulfonylureas were discontinued; HbA1c target <=6.5%.

canonical_statement: The standard-control arm pursued glucose control with glycated hemoglobin targets defined by local guidelines; participants using gliclazide modified release at entry were switched to another sulfonylurea if sulfonylurea therapy was continued.

concept.text: Standard glucose control according to local guidelines

exposures.details: Gliclazide modified release was replaced by another sulfonylurea if sulfonylurea therapy was required.

canonical_statement: The joint primary outcome combined major macrovascular events and major microvascular events.

concept.text: Combined major macrovascular and microvascular events

outcome.definition: First occurrence of either a major macrovascular event or a major microvascular event.

canonical_statement: Major macrovascular events were cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.

concept.text: Major macrovascular events

outcome.definition: Death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.

canonical_statement: Major microvascular events were new or worsening nephropathy or retinopathy, using prespecified renal and retinal definitions.

concept.text: Major microvascular events

outcome.definition: New or worsening nephropathy or new or worsening retinopathy as defined in the protocol.

canonical_statement: Severe hypoglycemia required transient central nervous system dysfunction that made the patient unable to self-treat and required another person's assistance.

concept.text: Severe hypoglycemia

outcome.definition: Transient CNS dysfunction with inability to self-treat, requiring help from another person.

canonical_statement: Primary end points and deaths were adjudicated by an independent End Point Adjudication Committee unaware of treatment assignment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An independent End Point Adjudication Committee, unaware of the group assignments, reviewed source documentation for all suspected primary end points and deaths.

canonical_statement: Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle and used unadjusted Cox proportional-hazards models; no adjustment for multiple statistical testing was made.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All analyses were conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle... No adjustment for multiple statistical testing was made.

canonical_statement: Because combined event rates were lower than expected after about 3 years, the investigators, while blinded to intervention effects, prespecified joint analysis of the two primary outcomes and extended glucose-control follow-up by 18 months.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: After a mean of approximately 3 years of follow-up, it became apparent that the event rates... were lower than expected... joint... analysis of the primary outcomes was prespecified, and... follow-up was extended... by 18 months...

canonical_statement: The trial had inadequate statistical power to reliably detect the macrovascular benefit expected from the achieved HbA1c separation because the annual macrovascular event rate was 2.2%, lower than the anticipated 3.0%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The annual rate of macrovascular events (2.2%) was lower than the anticipated rate of 3.0%... the ADVANCE trial did not have adequate statistical power to detect such an effect reliably.

canonical_statement: The low rate of retinal photocoagulation limited power to detect moderate effects of intensive glucose control on microvascular eye disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This low event rate limited the power of the study to detect any moderate effects of the intervention on microvascular eye disease.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that intensive glucose control to an average HbA1c of 6.5% reduced the combined macrovascular/microvascular outcome mainly through a roughly one-fifth reduction in renal complications, without demonstrated macrovascular benefit.
The trial was supported by Servier, the major financial sponsor, and the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia; Servier manufactures gliclazide modified release.

canonical_statement: Participating laboratories standardized HbA1c measurements against central laboratory reference values using WEQAS samples and laboratory-specific linear regression correction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Laboratories participating in ADVANCE underwent a standardization process using the Wales External Quality Assurance Scheme (WEQAS)... Results from the central lab were considered the gold standard values...
